liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Estimated Prophet** (1 review): Reviewer heard part of the second set on the radio and found Estimated strangely powerful [12]
- **Iko Iko** (1 review): The show ended with a smoking Iko Iko, then Knockin' with the Neville Brothers and Bangles [17]
- **Wharf Rat** (1 review): After the show, reviewer wandered by the river feeling like a Wharf Rat [17]
- **Hell In A Bucket** (1 review): Sound was adjusted early to balance Brent and Jerry; Bobby's steady vocals anchored this opener [21]
- **Little Red Rooster** (1 review): Reviewer hears a brooding solemnity in this performance [21]

## Setlist highlights

- **gd88-10-18 t01 Crowd**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [23]
- **gd88-10-18 t02 Hell In A Bucket**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [23]
- **gd88-10-18 t03 They Love Each Other**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [23]
- **gd88-10-18 t04 Little Red Rooster**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [23]
- **gd88-10-18 t05 Loser**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [23]
- **gd88-10-18 t06 Beat It On Down The Line**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [23]
- **gd88-10-18 t07 Greatest Story Ever Told**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [23]
- **gd88-10-18 t08 Peggy O**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [23]

## The recordings

- **gd1988-10-18.141504.schoeps.cmc3.mk41.pcm.mattes.miller.clugston.flac1644** (recommended): audience recording; 24 songs; 170 min [1]
- **gd1988-10-18.151615.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.voss.miller.t.flac16**: soundboard; 22 songs; 162 min [6]
- **gd1988-10-18.151208.ultramatrix.voss.miller.flac2496**: soundboard; 22 songs; 162 min [7]
- **gd88-10-18.sbd-matrix.leeds.17079.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 145 min; rated 3.68/5 by 19 [9]. Said about its sound: Calls the matrix poor: too much audience in the mix, with distracting echo on vocals and organ; Reviewer says the recording quality is pretty good, and the Bangles sounded decent alongside the band [13][19]
- **gd1988-10-18.115801.aud.encores.RSTERRAPIN.flac16**: audience recording; 2 songs; 13 min [10]

## Around the show

- Bangles came over from the George Michael Superdome show to join the Neville Brothers and band for the encores [15]
- Reviewer, from north Louisiana, was about ten feet from the band and was impressed by the parking lot scene and vendors [17]
- The Bangles were opening for George Michael at the Superdome that same night, then joined the Dead and Nevilles [22]
- Members of the Neville Brothers joined during Drums; the Bangles joined for the encores Iko Iko and Knockin' [1]
- Willie Green on drums and Art Neville on Hammond B3 joined, with the Bangles, for Iko Iko and Knockin' [6]
- Willie Green on drums and Art Neville on Hammond B3 joined for the encores with the Bangles [7]
- Reviewer found it a weird show and felt the band did not play especially well [15]
- Reviewer waited all night for Truckin', which was never played [20]
- The community previously had no encores in any format; this fills that gap [10]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1988-10-18.141504.schoeps.cmc3.mk41.pcm.mattes.miller.clugston.flac1644**: taped by Ted Mattes; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Source Info: Ted Mattes' Master Audience PCM (OTS); Scoeps CMC3/MK41 > Oade P/S > Sony PCM-F1 > Sony SL-2000; Tansfer Info: PCM (Sony SL-10)> Sony PCM-601ESD >… [1]
- **gd1988-10-18.151615.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.voss.miller.t.flac16**: taped by Recorded by Jim Voss (GD crew); transferred by All Transfers and Mastering By Charlie Miller  December 19, 2020; source: UltraMatrix SBD > Cassette Master (Sony TC-D5M/Maxell XLII-S) [6]. Also: UltraMatrix soundboard recorded by Jim Voss of the Dead's crew, with a patch source from Steven Leeds, Paul B and Kevin Tobin [6]
- **gd1988-10-18.151208.ultramatrix.voss.miller.flac2496**: taped by Jim Voss; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering By Charlie Miller  December 19, 2020; source: UltraMatrix SBD > Cassette Master (Sony TC-D5M/Maxell XLII-S) [7]. Also: Main source chain: UltraMatrix SBD to cassette master, VHS HiFi, DAT, then CD; Knockin' ending comes from a DAT master clone [7]
- **gd88-10-18.sbd-matrix.leeds.17079.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD(Healy Mix)>MC>HiFi VHS>DAT>CDR>CD WAVE>WAVE LAB>MKW>SHN (Seekable) [9]. Also: This matrix copy lacks the encores [11]
- **gd1988-10-18.115801.aud.encores.RSTERRAPIN.flac16**: taped by Randy Gardner; source: Encores Only, AUD > ? > FLAC [10]. Also: Audience-recorded encores, from tapes sent by Randy Gardner; the uploader remastered very difficult raw sources [10]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Kirsten Michel: [1988-10-18 Keifer Lakefront Arena, New Orleans, LA, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1988-10-18-keifer-lakefront-arena-new-orleans-la-usa/) [24]
- Fan art by LiveGRATEFUL.net: [Grateful Dead 1988-10-18 Tue Kiefer Lakefront Arena, University of New Orleans, New Orleans, LA](https://www.livegrateful.net/post/1418319548620/grateful-dead-1988-10-18-tue-kiefer) [25]
